course_name_original: Ampliación de Elasticidad y Resistencia de Materiales
course_name_en: Extension of Elasticity and Strength of Materials
prerequisites: Having taken Elasticity and Strength of Materials

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and abilities to apply the fundamentals of elasticity and strength of materials to the behavior of real solids.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Ability to analyze and synthesize.
Ability to learn and work autonomously.
Ability to solve problems.
Ability to apply knowledge to practice.

That students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competences usually demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and problem solving within their area of study.
Know how to calculate maximum and minimum principal stresses from principal axes.
Analyze plane stress and strain states and know how to calculate stresses in arbitrarily oriented planes.
Know how to apply the matrix method to calculate flat and three-dimensional beam structures.
Calculate the stresses of a thick beam under coupled bending and tensile forces.
Know how to calculate stress states in the walls of cylindrical pressure vessels.
Ability to dimension cylindrical pressure vessels.
Know how to calculate the stresses of a high-speed rotating disk.
Ability to calculate stresses in symmetric domes using membrane theory.
Ability to calculate stresses in a circular plate under the action of external loads producing bending.
Know how to calculate stress states of shells under the action of axisymmetric loads.
Know how to use CAD software for design and computational calculation.
Know how to simulate stress and strain states of flat structures built by bars and beams and know how to interpret the results.
Know how to write computational calculation reports.
Know how to check results calculated by CAD software with those obtained by the matrix method for structural calculation.
Know the most common terms in English.

syllabus_topics: Topic 1. Stress and strain state at a point. Equilibrium of the stress state within the body. Equilibrium of the stress state on the body's surface. Determination of stresses in arbitrarily oriented planes. Principal axes and principal stresses. Plane stress and strain. Limit stress states. Von Mises stress.
Topic 2. Verification of beams under oblique stress. Rectangular and circular beams. Moment diagrams in two planes.
Topic 3. Matrix calculation method for bar structures and beam structures, planar and three-dimensional. Stiffness method. Rotation and assembly of elemental matrices.
Topic 4. Thick-walled tubes. Fundamental equilibrium equations. Displacements, deformations, and stresses. Determination of stresses in composite tubes. Interference. Disks rotating at high speed.
Topic 5. Axisymmetric domes using membrane theory. Stress calculation. Hydrostatic loads.
Topic 6. Bending of circular plates subjected to symmetric loads. Fundamental equilibrium equations. Displacements, deformations, and stresses.
Topic 7. Bending of cylindrical shells under axisymmetric loads.
Practice 1. Introduction to programming matrix methods for solving 2D bar and beam problems (Excel)
Practice 2. Introduction to SOLIDWORKS modeling of 2D bar and beam problems.
Practice 3. Modeling of isostatic and hyperstatic 2D bar problems. Solidworks
Practice 4. Modeling of isostatic and hyperstatic 2D beam problems. Solidworks
Practice 5. Modeling of planar frame problems. Solidworks
Practice 6. Modeling of 3D structures problems. Solidworks
teaching_methods: Practical classes in the computational laboratory
Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools as learning support
Theoretical or problem-solving classes for the full group
Practical classes in the classroom for medium or full groups
Conducting seminars or other complementary activities for full or small groups
Attendance at tutorials, in-person and/or virtual, for small groups
Laboratory or computer lab practices for small groups
assessment_rules: For continuous assessment, a minimum grade of 5 out of 10 is required for each development test and each simulated task execution test. At least 80% of practical reports must be correct with a minimum grade of 5/10. If development tests are passed but practicals are not, the final grade will be 4.5. If development tests are failed but practicals are passed, the final grade will not exceed 3.0. For the single assessment, students must pass a development test (70%), a laboratory test (20%), and reports (10%), with specific minimums for each. Practical reports are mandatory for both modalities, and a minimum grade of 5/10 on the development test is required for practical report weighting.
